sentences.text: Learned Advocate for the appellant is absent.
The appeal is already admitted.
It appears that office has raised objection as to how respondent No.2 has been made a party respondent.
Respondent No.2 appears to be the victim.

The appellant stood prosecuted for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(k)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (for short "POCSO Act").

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Perusal of the judgment would show that after the appellant was held guilty he has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year.
Further, it has been stated that if the fine amount is recovered then it should be paid to the victim as compensation under Section 357(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short "Cr.P.C.").
2. We are guided by the Division Bench of this Court in Emperor V/s.
Chunilal Bhagwanji reported in AIR (29) 1942 Bombay 205(1).
It was the case under the old Cr.P.C. 2 apeal424.2021 Section 545 of then Cr. P.C. was equivalent to present Section 357(1) of Cr.P.C.

It was observed by this Court ".....where a person, whether the complainant or some one else, has been awarded compensation under S. 545, Criminal P.C., he ought to be served with notice of an appeal or revision application which may result in the order of compensation being set aside.
If he appears, it will be in the discretion of the Court to hear his advocate or to decline to do so.
But if he is served with notice, he can, at any rate, see that his view is placed before the Court by the advocate appearing for Government."

sentences.text: We may also consider Section 40 of the POCSO Act which gives a right to a child to take assistance of experts thereby a right is created in favour of the child or the guardian, as the case may be, to take assistance of a legal expert of their choice and the words used in Section 40 are "for any offence under this Act".

We may liberally interpret it, that it can be at any stage and at the stage of appeal also, when compensation has been awarded and in the appeal that part of the sentence is also challenged, then respondent No.2 has a right to put-forth her say and, therefore, she is a necessary party to the appeal.
We do not find any error committed by the learned Advocate for the appellant in making respondent No.2 as a party respondent.
There is absolutely no necessity to file any pursis or removal of the office objection in this regard.
3. Since the appeal is already admitted it appears that R and P was received by this Court at the time of suspension of sentence.
If paper book is not prepared then the office to 3 apeal424.2021 get paper book prepared as per rules.
The liberty is granted to the learned Advocate for the appellant to get the matter circulated after the paper book is received.
(MRS.VRUSHALI V.JOSHI,J.) (SMT. VIBHA KANKANWADI,J.) Signed by: MR. N.V.Tambaskar.
